changeset: M1.1 .sloodge document model (git diff app-shell doc-model)

blockers.what: `resolveZip64Sizes` honours a ZIP64 extended-information extra field (id 0x0001) unconditionally, whenever a declared size is 0xffffffff. fflate honours it only when a valid ZIP64 end-of-central-directory record exists: `z64hs` (fflate/lib/index.cjs:1846-1865) is gated on the `z` flag that `unzip` sets at index.cjs:2589-2597. A central-directory entry with sizes 0xffffffff plus a 0x0001 extra field, in an archive with *no* ZIP64 EOCD, is therefore read as small by our caps and as 4294967295/4294967295 by fflate.
blockers.why: PoC built and executed against the shipped defaults. A 307130-byte crafted file with one DEFLATE member: central header declares compressedSize=originalSize=0xffffffff, the 0x0001 extra field declares 5 inflated bytes and 306988 compressed, and the payload is 300 MB of zeros deflated. `scanCentralDirectory` resolves it to 5/306988, so every cap passes trivially (maxEntryBytes, maxTotalBytes, maxTotalCompressedBytes, and the sum-of-compressed vs file-length structural check all see ~300 kB). fflate then takes su=sc=4294967295, picks the `sc > 0.8 * su` sync branch at index.cjs:2625 and calls `inflateSync(..., { out: new u8(4294967295) })`. Measured inside vitest: `arrayBuffers` grew by 4096 MB and RSS by 292 MB, and `readDeck` ran to completion (returning `manifest-missing`, i.e. the member was fully materialized). The inflated payload is attacker-chosen up to 4 GB, and up to `maxEntries` members can do this within the 200 MB file cap, so this is the OOM-kill of the Electron main process that the module's docblock (store.ts:31-39) and the comment at store.ts:519-522 ("fflate allocates at most max(originalSize, compressedSize) per member ... the caps we just enforced are a real memory ceiling and not merely advisory") both promise cannot happen. Graded a blocker on the same reasoning r2 used for its blocker: readDeck has no production caller yet, but the module documents the guarantee as upheld and ships green tests asserting it, so the next person to wire it into an IPC handler will trust a control that does not exist. This is the second exploited instance of the divergence class r2 recorded in H2; the r3 fix closed only the locator axis (store.ts:307-328), and the same `z` flag that the fix reasoned about also gates per-entry extra-field resolution.
blockers.fix: Have `scanCentralDirectory` compute a `hasZip64` boolean (true only on the validated locator+record path at store.ts:316-328) and thread it into `resolveZip64Sizes`. When it is false, do not read the extra field at all: return `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` for any size declared 0xffffffff, exactly as the no-record fallback at store.ts:288-291 already does, so the caps reject the file. Add a regression test that crafts this shape (hand-rolled zip, no ZIP64 EOCD, 0xffffffff sizes plus a 0x0001 extra field) and asserts `too-large`, and a companion test that the same shape *with* a valid ZIP64 EOCD is still read correctly.

majors.what: The `allocates = compressionMethod === 0 ? Math.max(originalSize, compressedSize) : originalSize` branch — the core of the r2 blocker fix — is not pinned by any test. Reverting it to a bare `entry.originalSize` leaves all 156 tests green, including `tests/unit/document/store.test.ts:707`, the test named "caps a single STORED member by its compressed size, not its declared inflated size".
majors.why: Verified by reverting the branch in place and re-running `pnpm vitest run tests/unit/document/store.test.ts` — 55 passed, 0 failed. That test passes either way because the *separate* per-entry compressed cap at store.ts:484 fires first and produces a message containing `assets/alias-0.bin`, which is all the test asserts. The branch is nonetheless load-bearing: it is the only thing that makes a STORED member contribute to `maxTotalBytes`. Confirmed with a scratch test — `readDeck(storedZip(originalSize: 0), { maxEntryBytes: 1 MB, maxTotalBytes: 32 kB, maxTotalCompressedBytes: 1 GB })` returns `too-large` "inflates to over the 32768-byte limit" with the branch and `manifest-missing` without it. So the fix for r2's blocker is only partially revert-proof: fix B (sum-of-compressed vs file length) and fix C (zip64 locator strictness) each go red on revert, this one does not.
majors.fix: Add one case to the B2 suite using the existing `aliasedStoredZip(1, 0)` helper with `limits: { maxEntryBytes: 1024 * 1024, maxTotalBytes: 32 * 1024, maxTotalCompressedBytes: 1024 ** 3 }` and assert the message contains `inflates to over`. That isolates the effective-size computation from the per-entry compressed cap.

majors.what: `THEME_TOKEN_VALUE_FORBIDDEN` bans `<>{};@\`, both comment delimiters and control characters, but not parentheses and not a bare `//`. A token value of `url(//evil.example/beacon.png)` passes `assertSafeThemeToken` and is emitted verbatim into the slide's `<style>`.
majors.why: Confirmed by execution: `renderThemeBlock({ '--sl-bg': 'url(//evil.example/beacon.png)' })` emits `--sl-bg: url(//evil.example/beacon.png);`, and `--sl-bg` is consumed by `background: var(--sl-bg)` at starter-slide.ts:142 and :150, so the slide issues an outbound network request the moment it renders. `image-set(url(...))` and `var(--x, url(...))` pass too. That is a deck-open beacon and an IP disclosure driven by `theme/theme.json` inside an untrusted `.sloodge` (`ThemeFontsSchema` is a bare non-empty string and every theme object is a `z.looseObject`), and it directly contradicts SL-S01 as this file's own header states it at line 9: "zero subresources, zero network/storage APIs". The r3 denylist achieves exactly what its docblock claims — nothing that survives it can end the style element, the rule, the declaration or the sentinel comment — so this is a scope gap rather than a regression, and it is a major rather than a blocker for the same reason r2 graded the injection issue a major: `DEFAULT_THEME_TOKENS` is still the only caller, no theme-to-token mapper exists yet. The existing tests at starter-slide.test.ts:96-99 cover `red; background: url(x)` and `@import url(x)`, both of which are caught by the `;` and `@` rules, so the bare-`url()` case looks covered and is not.
majors.fix: Add `(` and `)` to the forbidden character class. No legitimate token this app emits needs them — a font stack such as `Inter, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif` is parenthesis-free, and colors, lengths and radii are too. Add a test asserting `url(//evil.example/x.png)` throws `ThemeTokenError`.

minors.what: Nit: the central-directory loop builds the full `CentralEntry[]` before `central.length > limits.maxEntries` is checked at line 446.
minors.why: Harmless for a 16-bit EOCD (count is capped at 65535 by the field width), but a ZIP64 record can declare an arbitrary count, and the loop only stops when `need` runs past the end of the file. A 200 MB archive of 46-byte headers yields ~4.5 M entry objects — a few hundred MB of transient allocation before the cap that exists to prevent it runs. Same shape as the r2 `readFile`-before-cap nit, which was fixed.
minors.fix: Reject as soon as `entries.length` exceeds `maxEntries` inside the loop, rather than after it.

minors.what: Nit: `claim` silently returns when a name is already in `zippable`, so the second writer's bytes are dropped without a word.
minors.why: Inconsistent with the surrounding design: packDeck deliberately *throws* `incomplete-bundle` for a missing slide body (line 684) and an orphan theme (line 671) precisely so a caller bug never becomes silent data loss. `manifest.theme` is a free-form `archivePath`, so a manifest pointing `theme` at a slide's own `slides/<id>.html` makes the theme claim win and the slide HTML vanish. Not reachable with a bundle this app produces, and the collision case is self-neutralizing today (a colliding theme path means the slide content *was* the theme JSON), which is why it is a nit rather than a major.
minors.fix: Throw `PackError('incomplete-bundle', ...)` on a collision between two distinct byte payloads, or at minimum name the loser in the error.

minors.what: Nit: `fflate` and `zod` are still direct carets rather than pnpm `catalog:` entries (carried over from r2).
minors.why: .claude/plans/init/11-tech-stack.md:93-102 makes the catalog the single source of truth and already lists `zod: ^4.4.3`; `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s catalog block has neither, and fflate has no row in that doc's dependency table. The deferral is now explicitly reasoned in store.ts:59-64, which is the right way to carry a known gap, so this stays a nit — but the doc is still the thing that is wrong.
minors.fix: Move both to the workspace catalog and add a fflate row to 11-tech-stack.md with the next dependency that lands.

verification.test: pnpm test — exit 0, 7 files / 156 tests passed

hypotheses_tested: H1: the r3 zip64 fix closed only the locator axis; fflate's `z` flag also gates per-entry ZIP64 extra-field resolution, which our scanner applies unconditionally. CONFIRMED and exploited — 307 kB file, caps told 5 inflated bytes, fflate allocated a 4096 MB ArrayBuffer and inflated 300 MB into it, readDeck ran to completion. Recorded as the blocker. Divergence first proven non-destructively with a filter callback: fflate reports `{"size":4294967295,"originalSize":4294967295}` for a member our scanner resolves to 5/306988.

H2: the r2 blocker fix is revert-proof. PARTIALLY REJECTED — reverting the sum-of-compressed vs file-length check reds `rejects many central entries aliasing one STORED local header`; reverting the zip64 locator strictness reds `rejects a zip64 locator whose record is out of bounds`; reverting the `max(originalSize, compressedSize)` STORED branch reds *nothing* (55/55 still pass). Recorded as major 1, with a scratch test proving the branch is load-bearing for `maxTotalBytes`.

H3: the theme-token denylist can be bypassed to reach a network or script context. PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — script/style escape is genuinely closed (`</style>`, `}`, `;`, `@`, `/*`, `*/`, control chars, over-length and non-`--[a-z0-9-]+` names all throw), but `url(//host/x)`, `image-set(url(...))` and `var(--x, url(...))` all pass and reach `background: var(--sl-bg)`. Recorded as major 2.

H4: the prototype discipline stops at deck.ts as it did in r2. REJECTED — `getSlide('constructor'|'toString'|'valueOf'|'__proto__')` all return undefined on a fresh deck; `slideMap` (deck.ts:68) rebuilds a null-prototype map on every `withSlides`; and even a hostile `__proto__` slide id (bypassing the schema regex, as M1.2's command layer could) round-trips as an ordinary own key through addSlide/updateSlide/slidesInOrder/removeSlide with `Object.prototype` unpolluted. Computed keys in `{ ...deck.slides, [entry.id]: entry }` use DefineOwnProperty, so the spread at deck.ts:222/307 is not a pollution vector either. `types.ts:325` re-keys at the parse boundary as claimed.

H5: cap arithmetic can be overflowed or bypassed on another axis. REJECTED for the axes tried — a directory marker is validated then skipped before it can contribute a size, and it is excluded from `wanted` so fflate never inflates it; duplicate central names are summed twice by the compressed accounting so aliasing under a shared name is still bounded; an unknown compression method takes `allocates = originalSize` in our scan and then fails fflate's `unknown compression type` and surfaces as `not-a-zip`; a STORED member with `sc` past the end of the file is clamped by fflate's `slc` (index.cjs:165-172); `resolveZip64Sizes` cannot loop forever because `offset` advances by at least 4.

H6: readDeck can be made to throw rather than return an error value. REJECTED — stat/readFile ENOENT and EISDIR both map to `not-found`/`io`, `scanCentralDirectory` throws only `ZipScanError` which is caught at line 442, `unzipAsync` rejection is caught at line 526 (and a fflate RangeError from an over-large allocation surfaces there as `not-a-zip`), and `strFromU8` on non-UTF-8 slide bytes is lossy rather than throwing (fflate only errors on strict UTF-8 decode, which this call site does not request).

H7: the r2 tmp-matching and TOCTOU nits regressed. REJECTED — `isTmpFor` (store.ts:197) matches only `<base>.<digits>.<8 base36>.tmp` and `tmpPathFor` pads to exactly 8 chars, both pinned by store.test.ts:281-289; `stat` now runs before `readFile` with a post-read re-check at store.ts:428 for the grow-under-us case.

H8: `createEmptyDeck` still emits a manifest referencing a theme file nobody writes. REJECTED — the `theme` key is omitted unless asked for (deck.ts:118), the rationale is documented at deck.ts:91-104, `packDeck` rejects orphan theme bytes (store.ts:670), and store.test.ts:186 asserts a create-save-reopen round trip produces `warnings: []`.
notes.confidence_derivation: Cap <=40 for the blocker; cap <=85 for the majors; lint + typecheck + test all run and green so no unverified cap; 8 hypotheses tested so no <90 cap; nothing unreadable. Landed at 28 rather than 40 because the blocker is the *second* exploited instance of the two-parser divergence class r2 recorded structurally, and one of the two majors shows the r2 blocker fix is only partially pinned by its own regression suite.
notes.summary: Nearly everything r2 asked for landed properly and holds under attack: the aliased-local-header PoC is dead by two independent controls, the prototype discipline is now structural rather than disciplinary (a hostile `__proto__` slide id round-trips as data with no pollution), the theme-token validator genuinely closes the style-element escape, createEmptyDeck no longer manufactures a phantom theme warning, and the TOCTOU and tmp-matching nits are fixed and pinned. The blocker is a second instance of the divergence r2 flagged as structural and the fix treated as one-off: fflate resolves a per-entry ZIP64 extra field only when a ZIP64 EOCD exists, our scanner resolves it always, and a 307 kB file that our caps measure at 5 inflated bytes drives a 4 GB allocation and 300 MB of real inflation. Thread the validated `hasZip64` flag into `resolveZip64Sizes`, add `(`/`)` to the token denylist, and add the one test that isolates the STORED effective-size branch.
